doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Waiting out the union card
summary: He explains the residency wait before getting his New York union card.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Can you explain that? What that meant?

Well you had to spend so much time in the area, in the city. You could take a job here and a job there, but you couldn’t take a steady job for about three months or something like that, or I think it was six months before you got your card or something like that. I finally got it.
To establish residency or something like that.
Yeah. And I mean they really checked on you.
Yeah. The union was not something to be trifled with at that time I guess. How much did it cost to join the union back then?
